outcomes: In a Go repository, each Go module is a component, named by its directory and its module path, found from go.work and go.mod
Each changed file maps to the module that holds it, and each module lists the repository modules it requires or replaces, so the change analysis can list the dependent modules
A Go test or coverage report that names a package or a file by its import path maps to the repository file and the module that holds it
Each module's go.mod gives the dependency versions it locks, so the change analysis can diff them between the base and the commit
nonGoals: Running go, reading the module cache or the network: the detector reads files only
Computing the changed and dependent components, the tests and coverage per component, the changed-line coverage and the dependency changes: the change analyses own them
Reading the content of test and coverage reports: the evidence readers own it
Running as its own extension over the workspace probe transport, which needs a host call that runs workspace probes outside a workspace

text: Each directory a root go.work uses is a component of source workspace;
each other go.mod found, skipping node_modules, vendor, testdata and dot or underscore directories, is one of source manifest.
Its id is its directory (. for the root), its name the module path, its ecosystem go.
A file belongs to the innermost component.
An unreadable or invalid manifest or directory, or a use outside the repository, is a diagnostic; a go.mod no grammar reads is a component without name or edges.

A component depends on each other component whose module path its go.mod requires, after the replace directives of its go.mod and of the root go.work, and on each component a local replace of its go.mod points to, resolved against the directory of the file holding it.
A require outside the repository, or an import without a require, is no edge; nor is the component itself.
A go.work member names its module path over other directories, else the first in path order.

An import path, as a go test -json event, a gotestsum or go-junit-report suite name and a go test -coverprofile file name write it, maps to the path below the component whose module path is its longest prefix on a slash boundary, and to that component;
the root module's own path maps to the root component and no file.
An import path no component's module path prefixes, or with an empty, . or .. element, maps to nothing.
A go.mod locks its requires, each with the version that the replace directives of the go.mod and of the root go.work at the same commit select, and whether it is indirect.
A require replaced by a local directory, or of a module the repository holds, is not locked.
Each component names its go.mod as its lockfile and its go.mod and go.sum as watched files.
Versions compare by Go's semantic version order.

The detection is also a workspace probe answer of @putnami/observe: one project per component, its module path and go.mod as source name and source file, its dependencies as component paths attributed to go-module, its go.mod and go.sum as watched files, the root go.work as a watched file.
The answer validates against the workspace protocol's probe rules.
